preparation.description: Durable preparation state for the run's preparation axis. This is an operational summary only; it never exposes connector-owned preparation input. It is not nullable: admission creates a run, its preparation, and its execution in one transaction and nothing deletes an axis on its own, so every readable run carries a summary. A row whose preparation is missing is corrupt — the Control Plane drops it from list reads and answers 404 for a single-run read, logging the fault — rather than reported with a null summary.

status.description: Preparation lifecycle. `preparing` means a preparer currently owns the claim; it is the preparation axis's own "in progress" state and is unrelated to the Runner, which is only submitted to once preparation reaches `submitted`.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the preparation phase began (a preparer first claimed the work); null while it is still pending. A retry that returns the row to pending and claims it again does not move it, so it is a safe start bound for the phase.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the preparation phase reached a terminal state (`submitted` or `failed`); null while it is pending or preparing. Distinct from `updated_at`, which also moves on claim heartbeats and input checkpoints and cannot mark the phase end.

status.description: The Runner lifecycle, retained under its established public name. `pending` means the run has been admitted but its prepared input has not yet been submitted to the Runner; preparation progress is reported separately by `preparation`. `skipped` means execution never ran because preparation failed; the reason is on `preparation`, not here. `uncertain` means a submission may have reached the Runner but its result could not be confirmed; a recovery replays it to resolve the run to `queued` or `failed`, so it is not a failure.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the prepared Runner input was accepted and execution began; null while the run is still pending, and also null for `skipped`, which is concluded without ever having started. Written once, so a recovery replay does not move it.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the execution axis reached a terminal state (`succeeded`, `failed`, or `skipped`); null while it is pending, queued, running, or uncertain. Together with `started_at` it times the phase (only when `started_at` is non-null, since `skipped` has an end without a start).

updated_at.description: Last time the execution axis was written: a polling confirmation, a state transition, or a submission/recovery write. This is the observation freshness the console reports ("observed Ns ago"), not a phase bound — use `started_at` and `finished_at` for that.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the publication phase began (the work was first claimed); null while it is pending, and null for `skipped`, which is concluded without ever having started. A retryable failure that returns the row to pending and claims it again does not move it.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the publication axis reached a terminal state (`published`, `failed`, or `skipped`); null while it is pending or publishing. It is set for every terminal outcome. The instant the result became visible is this field read together with `status: published`.

updated_at.description: Last time the publication axis was written, including claim heartbeats. This is the activity freshness the console reports, not a phase bound — use `started_at` and `finished_at` for that. Unlike them it keeps advancing while a long publication runs.
